buffered-n0: n == 0 returns the empty Slice with no file read, no rate-limiter call and no listener notification, even with a failing script

buffered-loop: allowed is RequestToken(n - read, 0, priority, nullptr, kRead) when priority != IO_TOTAL and a limiter is installed, else n (IO_TOTAL bypasses even an installed limiter; no limiter means allowed = n)

buffered-read: file_->Read(allowed, IOOptions(), &tmp, scratch + read, nullptr) with a fresh IOOptions per iteration (timeout 0, prio kIOLow 0, rate_limiter_priority IO_TOTAL 4, type kUnknown 7, empty property_bag, force_dir_fsync false, do_not_recurse false); the returned IOStatus is moved into the sret field by field, dropping subcode (+2) and scope (+6); the previous iteration's sret state_ is delete[]'d first

buffered-listeners: with listeners, start_ts is taken before the read and offset_ advances by tmp.size() ONLY through the notify fetch_add (no listeners means offset_ never moves on the buffered path); the FileOperationInfo carries the deep-copied status (Status::CopyState 0x61cf610) and each non-base listener's OnFileReadFinish (vtable slot 33) is called; base no-op listeners (0x6042c10) are skipped by the devirtualisation guard

direct-align: offset = offset_.fetch_add(n) up front; aligned_offset = offset & ~(alignment - 1); offset_advance = offset - aligned_offset; size = Roundup(offset + n, alignment) - aligned_offset; capacity = Roundup(size, alignment); raw buffer of capacity + alignment bytes

direct-loop: allowed is RequestToken(capacity - read, alignment, priority, nullptr, kRead) when the limiter applies, else size; file_->PositionedRead(aligned_offset + read, allowed, IOOptions(), &tmp, aligned_buf + read, nullptr); read += tmp.size(); break unless ok AND tmp.size() == allowed

direct-tail: r = min(read - offset_advance, n) when io_s is ok AND offset_advance < read, else 0; memcpy(scratch, aligned_buf + offset_advance, r); *result = Slice(scratch, r); the raw buffer is delete[]'d; IOSTATS_ADD(bytes_read, r); the tail runs on a short read with an ok status but NOT when io_s is non-ok
direct-listeners: offset_ advances by n up front AND by every chunk's tmp.size() through the notify fetch_add when listeners exist

observations: The main FDE has NO vendor census record, so no source hash can be bound the census way; the body hash is computed directly from the binary over the FDE range (0x6048e00..0x60497fd, 2557 B). The routine's identity is pinned by the .cold census symbol, which names SequentialFileReader::Read with the exact v8.1.1 signature (size_t n, Slice* result, char* scratch, Env::IOPriority).

The scratch[0]++ paranoid bump IS present in the binary (0x6049784: add BYTE PTR [rax],0x1), reached from the n == 0 check (jne 0x6049784). This closes the open unknown the #5986 ReadMore packet left behind. The bump runs before the first file read, so a successful read overwrites the bumped byte with the file's first byte; the bump is observable only when the read returns 0 bytes (a stale block then fails checksum) or in the event trace -- the live-engine check asserts it through the trace, not the final scratch.

The buffered path advances offset_ ONLY when listeners exist (the single lock xadd at 0x6049127 lives inside the notify block); without listeners offset_ never moves on the buffered path. The direct path advances offset_ by the full n up front (lock xadd at 0x60492c7) and then again by every chunk's tmp.size() when listeners exist -- so with listeners the direct path double-counts the read bytes in offset_.

The sret move drops the subcode and scope bytes: the binary moves code (2 bytes @+0), severity/retryable/data_loss (+3..+5) and state_ (+8) from the callee's Status into the sret, but never the subcode byte (+2) or the scope byte (+6), so the returned status always has subcode 0 and an unwritten scope byte (0 in practice, since callers zero the slot first).

The IOOptions is built fresh on the stack for every file call: the merged immediates pin timeout 0 + prio 0 + rate_limiter_priority 4 in one 0x400000000 qword at +0x08, type 7 at +0x10, and the property_bag as an empty unordered_map (bucket count 1, element count 0, max load factor 1.0); the _Hashtable dtor (0x5d36110) runs right after each call.

The direct-path else branch for allowed really is `allowed = size`, not `capacity - read`: the upstream else branch asserts buf.CurrentSize() == 0 and takes the whole window. The buffered-path else branch really is `allowed = n`, not `n - read`. Both are confirmed by the binary's jumps (cmp $0x4,%ecx; je to the bypass) and by the upstream source.

The listener notification devirtualises the empty base implementation: each listener's slot-33 entry is compared against 0x6042c10 (endbr64; ret) via LEA (0x60491fc, 0x6049650) and the call is skipped on a match; only real handlers receive the FileOperationInfo.

The tail runs on a short read with an ok status (0x6049758 jumps to the tail at 0x60496dc) but NOT when io_s is non-ok: an error after a good chunk leaves r = 0 even though bytes were read into the aligned buffer.

The unidentified caller FDE 0x60d4cf0..0x60d4f62 has NO vendor census record; it reads 0x2000 bytes with a priority forwarded from its caller. Its enclosing function is unidentified -- a follow-up packet can pin it.

Upstream RocksDB v8.1.1 confirms the packet on every point (read live this cycle): file/sequence_file_reader.cc Read step for step (buffered bump + loop + Slice(scratch, read); direct fetch_add + align + PositionedRead loop + memcpy tail; IO_TOTAL bypasses the rate limiter), file/sequence_file_reader.h member order (file_name_, file_, offset_, listeners_, rate_limiter_), Read signature, use_direct_io, NotifyOnFileReadFinish, ShouldNotifyListeners, env/file_system_tracer.h FSSequentialFilePtr selection and FSSequentialFileTracingWrapper layout. Correction to the assumed path: the file is file/sequence_file_reader.cc, not util/sequence_file_reader.cc (that path 404s at v8.1.1).

One check bug was caught and fixed in-cycle (not in-PR): the live-engine check asserted scratch[0] == data[0]+1 after a successful 100-byte read, but the read overwrites the bumped byte with the file's first byte; the check now asserts the bump through the event trace (scratch starts zeroed, so the bumped value is 1). The model itself was correct.

Two model bugs were caught and fixed in-cycle (not in-PR) while writing the test suite. (1) File._entry_status ignored the entry-level 'state' and 'ok' fields: every returned Status had a null state_, so the previous-state delete[] and the info.status deep-copy paths were never exercised (0 prev_status_state_freed / info_status_state_freed events across all 2,400 cases). The entry-level 'state' is now the Status state_ fallback and 'ok': False with no 'status' dict returns a generic IOError (code 1); the ledger now carries 8 distinct non-null states and both free paths fire. (2) The 'multi-chunk' buffered/direct cases never actually looped: without a limiter allowed == n (buffered) or size (direct), so a short first chunk breaks the loop at once and the later chunks were never reached. The multi-chunk, error-on-third-chunk, state-on-second-chunk, script-exhaustion and direct error-after-good cases now use a rate limiter (IO_LOW) so the loop genuinely continues across chunks.
